headline: High-risk autonomous coding agent paired with a customer-support bot creates dangerous default write, leakage, and compliance pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, MCP, Slack, and repo content by default, so attacker-controlled text can reach its instruction parser. Rasa can receive messages from Slack/Messenger-style channels, creating a plausible bridge if Devin posts content into shared threads or tickets. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Devin posts untrusted text into Slack, Jira, or Notion that Rasa later consumes as dialogue or workflow input
IF a shared MCP server or ticket thread is configured between the agents
mitigations: Disable any shared Slack/Jira/Notion handoff between the agents
Add a strict instruction/content delimiter before Rasa ingests Devin-authored text
Route Devin outputs through a human review step before posting
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and can write to cloud workspace files and integrations. Rasa is a chat bot with allowlisted egress and multiple messaging surfaces, so if Devin-sourced sensitive content is forwarded into Rasa, leakage to external channels is plausible. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so severity is high due to broad default exposure and uncertain containment.
conditions: IF Devin forwards repo secrets, chat, or docs into any Rasa-connected channel
IF Rasa is connected to an external messaging platform with user-visible transcripts
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared conversation or ticket payloads
Restrict Rasa channels to a test workspace
Turn off transcript forwarding from Devin to messaging tools
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, and git modification; Rasa can also participate in networked workflows through messaging integrations. If both touch the same repo, ticket, or shared workspace, Devin can overwrite state while Rasa emits conflicting actions or messages. Because Devin explicitly supports parallel sessions and shared integrations, the conflict risk is default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository, ticket queue, or shared workspace
IF Devin and Rasa can write to the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or queues per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state
Use branch-per-agent and merge only after review
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can generate code, tickets, and messages; Rasa can turn incoming text into dialogue actions. If Rasa treats Devin output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing responses or workflow actions. The path exists in default integrations, but Rasa can also be configured to verify inputs, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes Devin-generated text without validation
IF Devin-generated facts are used as the source for customer-facing replies or tickets
mitigations: Require human approval for Devin-authored facts before Rasa uses them
Add schema validation to Devin outputs before ingestion
Log and compare Devin claims against source data
requires-engineering: add automated verification against authoritative systems

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while Rasa handles text/voice across messaging platforms. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated customer data is routed through both. No specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is sent through Devin and then persisted in Rasa-connected channels
IF the deployment requires a specific residency, retention, or deletion policy that the two systems do not share
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared agent workflows
Shorten transcript retention in messaging channels
Document a single retention owner for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion controls across both vendors
